thread:
tess_sales: Heads-up — Acme asked for a committed capacity proposal. They expect ~3,000,000 tokens/day (sustained) and a ~1,200,000 token peak hour. Hard SLO: p95 latency <300ms for the chat route. They want reserved GPUs, burst slots, and a preheat/runbook. Any quick presales til we draft the one-pager?

raj_sol: Quick math: 3,000,000 tokens/day ≈ 34.7 tokens/sec sustained. Peak hour 1.2M tokens ≈ 333 tokens/sec. For rdl-13b quantized-like variants our ballpark is 40–60 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batching and KV hit-rate. Using 50 tps/GPU -> naive peak GPUs = 333/50 ≈ 6.7 → round up to 7. Add safety for context length and tail latency.

maria_infra: Practical recommendation (presales): reserved pool = 5 GPUs + burst pool = 3 GPUs. Rationale: 5 reserved → ~250 tps baseline, 3 burst → +150 tps peak = 400 tps total headroom. That covers 333 tps peak with room for short spikes and reduces queueing. Note: if customers use many long-context sessions, effective tps drops; KV cold-warm transition can reduce throughput by 25–45% initially.

maria_infra: Autoscale policy suggestion (use as example in the runbook):

```json
{
  "autoscale_policy": "queue_and_latency",
  "min_reserved": 5,
  "max_total_gpus": 8,
  "scale_up_trigger": {
    "queue_ms_above": 150,
    "p95_latency_ms_above": 250
  },
  "scale_step_gpus": 1,
  "cooldown_seconds": 90
}
```

raj_sol: Also recommend per-tenant rate caps and a lightweight backpressure header so the app can degrade request rate gracefully. For presales pricing note: recommend commit = 5 reserved + 3 burst. Ballpark commit discount vs pure on-demand ~30–38% depending on billing term and burst mix — include exact numbers in the pricing worksheet.

jon_prod: Preheat/runbook idea: nightly KV prewarm hitting top prompt templates + representative user prefixes, plus a short warmup run 15–30min before peak hour. Example preheat script snippet we can drop in the doc: 

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# simple prewarm: hit top templates + user prefixes
for tpl in $(cat top_templates.txt); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rdl-13b-q","input":"'$tpl'"}' >/dev/null &
done
# wait for background warmups to finish
wait
```

jon_prod: Add a short section describing expected degradation: if burst pool exhausted, route hits fall back to quantized-lower-capacity replicas (higher latency / lower quality). Document this fallback order and expected p95 ranges in SOW.

maria_infra: AZ and spot notes: recommend Dedicated spread across 2 AZs for resilience. If customer wants spot-backed burst to save cost, add +30% reserved headroom in the plan to account for potential spot reclamation; or prefer mixed burst strategy (1–2 dedicated burst + remainder spot).

raj_sol: Edge case: concurrent cold long-context sessions can cause memory pressure and KV eviction → brief latency spikes. Mitigations: enforce per-session max_context_tokens (soft cap), apply a short token-rate limiter per session, and surface a Retry-After or backpressure header.

deploy_bot: perf-matrix.csv uploaded to #sales-assets (link: https://redwood.internal/sales-assets/perf-matrix-rdl13b.csv)

tess_sales: Action items before we send to Acme: @raj_sol produce the one-page sizing + pricing table; @maria_infra draft the preheat + autoscale JSON + short runbook; @jon_prod write the fallback/SLO degradation blurb for SOW and the security questionnaire; I'll collate and respond to the security Qs. Target: internal review by EOD Thursday. :thumbsup:
